steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Finance cannot reconcile instance uptime. A metered machine in an account dedicated to one customer belongs to that customer regardless of which customer its tags name, including when they name none. A shared-account machine may belong to several customers and its uptime must be divided evenly among tenants genuinely onboarded for that account; unknown or unplaceable usage stays off the bill. The onboarding records in the metering bucket beside the account list identify billable customers. Update the metering sweep so published uptime follows those rules. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

steps.message:
The implementation is complete and verified:

**Changes made:**

1. **`src/utils/aws/s3.ts`** — added `listDocumentKeys(bucket, prefix)` which walks pagination so the sweep never reads a truncated view of the onboarding records.

2. **`src/onboarding/entities/customerOnboarding.entity.ts`** (new) — models the per-customer onboarding records that sit beside the account list in the metering bucket (`customerId`, `accounts: [{accountId, dedicated?}]`), loads them all (tolerating unreadable/invalid records), and `buildAccountTenancy()` turns them into a per-account view: which customers are genuinely onboarded for the account and whether the account is dedicated to exactly one of them (contested "dedicated" claims fall back to shared).

3. **`src/microservices/ec2InstanceDataGatherer/ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.ts`** — the sweep now attributes each metered instance via `attributeInstance()`:
   - dedicated account → all uptime to that customer, whatever (or nothing) the tags name;
   - shared account → uptime split evenly among tagged tenants that are actually onboarded for that account (unknown names filtered out);
   - nothing placeable (no tag on a shared account, only unknown names, or an account with no onboarded customers) → left off the bill with a warning.

**Verified against the emulator** (`dim-uptime-sandbox`): `cus_harbor` 0.291666655 (3 dedicated-account instances + half of the shared one), `cus_lattice` 0.124999995 (half the shared one + its own), and the untagged shared instance dropped. Added `ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.spec.ts` covering dedicated, even split, unknown tenants and unplaceable usage — all 5 pass; lint clean; remaining unit-suite failures (billing, token-consumer) are pre-existing and unrelated.
